MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 24, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:01 p.m., on January 24, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on January 19, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:04 pm)
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimant: Busan: Agency Claimed Against -
  City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph
  (2) of Subdivision (d) Section 54956.9 (1 case)

RECESS AND RECONVENE TO CLOSED SESSION

At the hour of 5:02 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:01 pm with all City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  January 24, 2023
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council was given updates but no reportable
actions were given.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Mission Viejo Nadadores Diver Anna Lemkin for Claiming Gold at the FINA
  Junior World Championships in Montreal

  Mayor Goodell presented certificate of commendation to Anna Lemkin.

P2. Check Presentation From the 2nd Annual Konrad Reuland Charity Tennis/Pickleball
  Tournament to Big Brothers Big Sisters

  Received presentation.

P3. Presentation on Providence Mission Hospital Expansion

  Received presentation from Chief Executive, Seth Teigen.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jim Leach, M.V.: Gave a brief report on the recycle water main break at the intersection of
Marguerite and Mustang Run near Trabuco Hills High School. The Water District is working with
the City on all required specifications and there was no environmental impact.

Nancy Larkin, M.V.: Spoke on the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) that is being built in her
neighborhood. She pointed out that the front door is now facing Silleros which is not a residential
street. Stated that the character of her neighborhood is changing.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Recapped his comments from the January 10 meeting, and asked again why
the city is defending the individuals in this case. Asked that Council Member Bucknum recuse
herself from all discussions on this matter since she is a defendant. Voiced concern on the taxpayers
and the City dollars and asked for an explanation on why the City continues to appeal Judge
Shwarm’s ruling.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Spoke on the coyote problem in his community of Casta del Sol.
Suggested we trap and euthanize them.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Requested the City Council would benefit to adopt a code of ethics and laid
out specifics of her plan for a Code of Ethics.
City Council Minutes  2  January 24, 2023
 Hector Ruiz, M.V.: He commented on Consent Calendar Item #5 on speed limits and thanked the
City Council for adopting this Ordinance.

Juan Gonzalez, M.V: Thanked the re-elected Council and the new council. As an employee of
Southern California Gas, he spoke on the high price of natural gas and explained the process of the
gas hike. He outlined how residents can lower their gas bill. He encouraged residents having trouble
paying their gas bill to call (800) 427-2200.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Thanked the City for the Pacific Symphony Concert this past summer. Voiced
concern over safety at such a large event in light of mass shootings throughout the country. Spoke
in favor of metal detectors at large community events.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Requested for a specific plan for the Core Area. Asked how La Paz and
Muirlands will be affected with the traffic down to Marguerite Parkway and suggested that it needs
to be included in the specific plan.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke on her comments from the January 10 Council meeting and criticized
the City Attorney. She asked on what legal authority the right to proceed without acknowledging
the voices of two new council members. She accuses the majority City Council and City Attorney
of interfered with the 2018 and 2020 elections.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 10, 2023, as
  presented.

2.  General Check Register dated January 6, 2023 in the amount of $3,356,230.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Golf Check Register dated January 6, 2023 in the Amount of $200,186.80

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  January 24, 2023
 4.  Proposed Amendment to Existing Lease Submitted by Sequoia Development Services,
  Inc. on behalf of Verizon Wireless in Conjunction with an existing Wireless
  Telecommunication Facility on a 60-foot light standard at William S. Craycraft Park,
  23551 Coronel Drive

  Approved and authorized the City Manager to execute the amended lease.

5.  2022 Citywide Speed Limit Update

  Adopted Ordinance 23-348 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Regarding Prima Facia Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

6.  Proposed Amendment to Existing Lease Submitted by Rolon Culver of MD7 on behalf
  of AT&T Mobility for an amendment to an existing lease agreement for an unmanned
  wireless telecommunications facility on a Southern California Edison (SCE) Tower
  generally located east of Olympiad Road between Jeronimo Road and Escratron, and
  north of Beebe Park, on City owned property at 24095 Olympiad Road, in the R
  (Recreation) zone

  Approved and authorized the City Manager to execute the amended lease.

7.  Fourth Amendment to Agreement with Matrix Imaging for Document Scanning
  Services

  Approved the Fourth Amendment to agreement with Matrix Imaging for an additional
  $26,300 resulting in a total not-to-exceed amount of $126,300 for Document Scanning
  Services and extend the term through June 30, 2023.

8.  Storm Drain Atlas Update (CIP 20243)

  Approved the Third Amendment to contract with Nobel Systems, Inc. in an amount not to
  exceed $5,200 for additional design services related to the update of the existing storm drain
  atlas of the City's GIS system.

9.  2023 Community Services Grant Program and Routine Funding Procedure
  Recommendations

  Approved the 2023 Community Services Grant Program Allocations and Routine Funding
  Procedures.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

10. Comprehensive User Fee Study

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and Willdan Consultant Toni Thrasher gave the
staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  January 24, 2023
 The Mayor opened the Public Hearing at 7:21 pm.

There being no public comment the Mayor closed the Public Hearing at 7:21 pm.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
Resolution 23-03 Amending and Augmenting the City of Mission Viejo Master Fee Schedule.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to rescind the
$200 piano rental fee at city facilities.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  Bucknum
ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

11. Municipal Code Update on Section 2.06.050 and Section 2.06.060 of Chapter 2.06 of
  Title Two of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Commission Selection and
  Removing Term Limits

City Attorney Bill Curley gave a brief staff report.

Hector Ruiz, M.V.: Asked the City Council to reconsider adding an anti-nepotism statement in the
ordinance.

Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to introduce
Ordinance 23-349 to Amending Sections 2.06.050 and 2.06.060 of Chapter 2.06 of Title Two of
the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Commission Selection and Removing Term Limits.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Mayo Kelley, and Ruesch
NOES:  Vasquez
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  January 24, 2023
 NEW BUSINESS

12. 2023-2025 Pre-Budget Discussion

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas gave the staff report.

The following requests and actions were made by Council Members for the 23-25 Budget
consideration.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley asked that Barbadanes Park be renovated in the 23/25 budget for the second
year and Craycraft Park in the 25/27 budget.

Council Member Ruesch asked that a 300-400 seat indoor Community be in the budget discussion.
Allocate enough funds in this next budget. Council Member Bucknum agreed with a public/private
partnership.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to authorize
staff to process contract extensions for Group I Infrastructure Maintenance Annual Routine
Maintenance Contracts and proceed with bidding process for contracts in Group II.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

Council Member Vasquez asked for an increase in subsidies for Kids Factory. Council Member
Bucknum asked Director Nix to include the scholarship program for Mission Viejo residents in the
budget for kid’s factory.

Director Dyas outlined future unfunded projects and programs that will need to be discussed for
consideration:

Corp Yard Facility Replacement
Core Area Vision Plan Phase II
Core Area Specific Plan
Public Safety Security Camera Network
2008 Olympic Planning
Others?

Mayor Goodell stated that a Specific Plan for the Core Area is something that needs to be focused
on this year. In addition, he stated that the Oso Creek Golf Course and Open Space area second
phase needs to be considered. He suggested additional parking, pickle ball courts, more food and
beverage options. He requested budget numbers. He also commented on the upcoming 2028
Olympics and to promote our sports tourism around the world to bring teams here for training
facilities.

City Council Minutes  6  January 24, 2023
 Council Member Bucknum requested that we look for grant funding opportunities for the core area
specific plan and security cameras. She suggested for the security cameras, we partner with the
County and adjacent communities since we are a gateway city to other communities so that the cost
doesn’t fall just on Mission Viejo.

Council Member Vasquez agreed with Council Member Ruesch on a community theater. She asked
to look into cost to build a playground and/or other amenities at La Mancha Park. Council Member
Vasquez pointed out different traffic situations around the City. City Manager Wilberg explained
theses concerns on traffic can be handled outside of the budget.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated she was interested in the public safety security camera network and
a core area specific plan is something to look at but would like more information on it. She also
endorsed the community theater.

Council Member Ruesch stated there is a great groundswell of funding grants and patrons of the art
may be likely to be involved for a community theater. He believes it’s a win-win for all of us to
investigate outside funding. He spoke in support of a place where Olympians come and train to
give the City better visibility and continue our mark as being an Olympic City.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

13. Oso Creek Water Reclamation Plant Facility and Construction of the Corp Yard
  Administration/Storage Building

  Received presentation from Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay.

14. Appointment to the Mission Viejo Nadadores Foundation Committee

  The Mayor appointed himself to the Mission Viejo Nadadores Foundation Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she finished up the State of the City filming for the
2022 year-end review. She commented on the art project in the Vibrations Tunnel along the Oso
Creek trail as well as the Lakeside Lookout. Council Member Bucknum attended the swearing-in
of Congresswoman Young Kim at the Nixon Library. She announced that this Friday the South
Orange County Sober Living Task Force will be meeting and she thanked both Assembly Members
Kate Sanchez and Laurie Davies. Council Member Bucknum asked staff to look into an ordinance
to allow chickens in residents yards. She would like a limited number and asked for the legalities.
City Council Minutes  7  January 24, 2023
 She stated that she does not want extra work for Animal Services. Lastly, she wished her grandson
Desmond a happy sixth birthday.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch stated he attended Association of California Cities – Orange County
(ACCOC) orientation and a briefing from the Sheriff’s Department. He mentioned that he has been
spending more time with the Chamber of Commerce. Council Member Ruesch reported that he
will continue to attend Lake Mission Viejo meetings and continue the good work between the City
and Lake for joint events. He stated he attended the live music performance this past Friday at Oso
Creek Golf Course. Council Member Ruesch commented on the public speaker regarding coyotes
being the only predator in the City and stated that mountain lions are also in the area. He mentioned
the rising cost of gas and electricity and asked if staff could provide at an upcoming council meeting
a brief look at how the City is conserving energy. Lastly, he thanked Staff and the Council for
allowing him to push forward the idea of a community theater.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated she also attended the ACCOC orientation. She took her youngest
daughter to the Meet and Greet for the Fire Fighters and indicated that her daughter enjoyed it and
that the even was well attended. Council Member Vasquez attended the Sheriff’s briefing and
commented that we need to keep into consideration all public safety agencies as to the rising costs
and budgets. She stated she went to her first Orange County Financing Housing Trust Meeting, but
it was continued due to lack of a quorum. She met with Principal Odebunmi of Bathgate
Elementary and the Principal of Viejo Elementary School. Council Member Vasquez also attended
the Meet and Greet with the Chamber of Commerce. Lastly, she stated she has two more
appointments with principals at Carl Hankey and Capo Valley High School in District 3.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that there will be an upcoming 20th Anniversary Celebration of
the Community of Character Program .

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell also attended Congresswoman Young Kim’s swearing-in ceremony. He announced
that he was appointed yesterday at the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA); re-
appointed to the Orange County Council of Governments Executive Committee on OCTA’s behalf,
Southern California Association of Governments Regional Committee and Transportation
Committee, Executive Committee of OCTA, Environmental Oversight Committee and Legislative
Chairman of the OCTA Committee. Lastly, he asked the City Attorney if it is legal to kill a coyote
in California. The City Attorney clarified the law in California and pointed out that two incidents
within the city were due to the residents trying to rescue their unleashed dog from a coyote’s mouth
and were bit.

ADJOURNMENT AT 10:30 PM TO TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 2023, AT 5:00 P.M.

City Council Minutes  8  January 24, 2023
 ______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 14, 2023

City Council Minutes  9  January 24, 2023
